title: Netherlands – Insurance services – WGA Eigenrisicodrager verzekering Gemeente Oude IJsselstreek
description: Ingeval van WGA eigenrisicodragerschap is de werkgever rechtstreeks verantwoordelijk voor de financiering van de aan de werkgever toe te rekenen WGA uitkeringen (tot maximaal 10 jaar na toekenning). Tevens gaat de re-integratieplicht na toekenning van een WGA uitkering over van UWV naar werkgever. Ter afdekking van de risico’s bij WGA eigenrisicodragerschap wenst Opdrachtgever een WGA Eigenrisicodrager Verzekering af te sluiten. Het betreft hier een private verzekering t.b.v. financiering van de aan de werkgever toe te rekenen WGA Vast en WGA flex uitkeringen. Opdrachtgever heeft op peildatum 1 september 2026 in totaal 362 werknemers in dienst. De verwachte WIA loonsom in 2026 bedraagt circa € 20,5 miljoen. Voor de inschatting van het risico en het vaststellen van de condities stelt de Aanbestedende dienst een beveiligd Excel document ter beschikking met geanonimiseerde personeelsgegevens, opgave zieke medewerkers en WIA instroom. Dit Excel bestand kan opgevraagd worden bij de gemeente Oude IJsselstreek door een verzoek hiertoe in te dienen op het e-mailadres aanbesteding@oude-ijsselstreek.nl . Dit Excel bestand wordt alleen verstrekt aan belangstellenden met een vergunning van de AFM voor het uitvoeren van het verzekeringsbedrijf conform de Wet Financieel Toezicht (of daarmee vergelijkbare wet- en regelgeving in het buitenland) en die een WGA eigenrisicodrager verzekering in het productassortiment voeren.

title: Framework for Drawdown Technical Assistance - Transaction Advisory, Finance and Investment Support (BRAVE-IS)
description: DAI Global UK is seeking proposals from firms to provide transaction advisory, finance and investment support to the Building Resilience and Addressing Vulnerability to Emergencies - Institutional Strengthening (BRAVE-IS) programme in Pakistan. BRAVE-IS is a multi-year (2026-2029) technical assistance programme funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO). Background Pakistan is among the countries most exposed to climate and disaster risk. The binding constraint on resilience investment is not policy but capability: government institutions lack the instruments and in-house capacity to turn identified needs into investable propositions that public, international and private financiers will fund. Scope BRAVE-IS will appoint one firm under a Time and Materials drawdown framework, from which it can mobilise experts and, where needed, complete delivery teams. Work will be commissioned through individual task requests. Expertise is required in: Transaction advisory and project structuring, including PPP and blended finance Feasibility, financial modelling and economic appraisal Investment pipeline development and project preparation Private sector engagement and investment mobilisation Institutional and embedded delivery support within federal and provincial government bodies Support must strengthen, not substitute for, government capacity, and tools and models must be handed over for continued use. Personnel will work in Islamabad, Lahore, Karachi and Peshawar, with travel elsewhere in Pakistan as required. Contract The initial period runs from date of award to 31 March 2027, extendable subject to programme requirements, performance and FCDO approval. No minimum volume of work is guaranteed. This is an open competition and rates are sought for locally based personnel. How to apply Submit one email to brave-is@dai.com with the subject line "BRAVE-IS-001 - Proposal - [Firm name]", attaching two separate PDF files: (1) a technical submission of no more than nine pages, with CVs as an annex, and (2) a financial proposal giving daily fee rates only for five personnel levels. Proposals will be scored 80% technical and 20% financial and must remain valid for 90 days. Key dates Clarification questions: by 9 October 2026, by email to brave-is@dai.com with the subject line "BRAVE-IS-001 - Clarification Question - [Firm name]" Proposal deadline: 20 October 2026, 17:00 Pakistan Standard Time (13:00 UK time) Please read the full RFP (reference BRAVE-IS-001) before applying. Late submissions will not be considered. DAI reserves the right to cancel the procurement or make no award.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.3 - How can we use technology to demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy business practices?
description: Zero Waste Scotland is seeking an innovative technology solution that helps businesses demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy practices and attract investment. Existing assessment tools often overlook benefits including (but not limited to) supply chain resilience, resource security, customer retention and reduced exposure to market shocks. We are looking for an intuitive, evidence-based tool that integrates the wider benefits into business and investment decisions, while generating insights to inform future support and policy development. The solution should build business and investor confidence, help accelerate adoption of circular practices and support Scotland's transition to a sustainable, circular economy.

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.4 - How can technology improve both the efficiency and the patient experience in NHS transport, starting with renal services?â
description: With over 273,000 people in Scotland living with Stage 3-5 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), including 2,000 receiving dialysis treatment, and demand expected to increase fivefold over the next decade, improvements to dialysis transport across NHS Scotland are urgently needed. Dialysis journeys account for more than 40% of all non-emergency patient transport activity, costing 9.1 million GBP annually. Yet current arrangements can be inconsistent, creating avoidable pressures for patients, providers and NHS services. NHS Scotland is seeking innovative, patient-centred and sustainable solutions that improve reliability, efficiency and patient outcomes, while reducing administrative burden and delivering better value for money.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?
description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isnât readily available (or isnât trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotlandâs Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 â 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individualâs âcircle of supportâ. This âcircle of supportâ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services â and if possible, create a âfeedback loopâ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isnât readily available (or isnât trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotlandâs Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 â 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individualâs âcircle of supportâ. This âcircle of supportâ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services â and if possible, create a âfeedback loopâ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.3 - How can we use technology to demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy business practices?
description: Zero Waste Scotland is seeking an innovative technology solution that helps businesses demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy practices and attract investment. Existing assessment tools often overlook benefits including (but not limited to) supply chain resilience, resource security, customer retention and reduced exposure to market shocks. We are looking for an intuitive, evidence-based tool that integrates the wider benefits into business and investment decisions, while generating insights to inform future support and policy development. The solution should build business and investor confidence, help accelerate adoption of circular practices and support Scotland's transition to a sustainable, circular economy.

The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isnât readily available (or isnât trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotlandâs Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 â 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individualâs âcircle of supportâ. This âcircle of supportâ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services â and if possible, create a âfeedback loopâ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.3 - How can we use technology to demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy business practices?
description: Zero Waste Scotland is seeking an innovative technology solution that helps businesses demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy practices and attract investment. Existing assessment tools often overlook benefits including (but not limited to) supply chain resilience, resource security, customer retention and reduced exposure to market shocks. We are looking for an intuitive, evidence-based tool that integrates the wider benefits into business and investment decisions, while generating insights to inform future support and policy development. The solution should build business and investor confidence, help accelerate adoption of circular practices and support Scotland's transition to a sustainable, circular economy.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.4 - How can technology improve both the efficiency and the patient experience in NHS transport, starting with renal services?â
description: With over 273,000 people in Scotland living with Stage 3-5 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), including 2,000 receiving dialysis treatment, and demand expected to increase fivefold over the next decade, improvements to dialysis transport across NHS Scotland are urgently needed. title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?
description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isnât readily available (or isnât trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotlandâs Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 â 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individualâs âcircle of supportâ. This âcircle of supportâ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services â and if possible, create a âfeedback loopâ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

title: Lukituksen uusiminen (16 kohdetta)
description: Lukituksen uusiminen (16 kohdetta) MEKAANINEN LUKITUS Sarjoituksen kohteena on 16 asuinkiinteistöä. Kohteiden mekaaninen lukitus uusitaan Abloy Easy - järjestelmällä. Sylinterit uusitaan, vanhat lukkorungot ja helat säilytetään. Urakoitsija on velvollinen tutustumaan kohteisiin omatoimisesti ennen tarjouksen antamista ja varmistamaan lukituskaavioiden ajantasaisuus. Jätekatokset, piharakennukset, postilaatikot yms. lukitukset kuuluvat urakkaan kohteissa, joissa nämä ovat ennestäänkin lukittuja. Urakkaan kuuluu lisäksi lukkojen telkien ja avainpesien (käyttölukot, varmuuslukot, pitkäsalvat) voitelu ja ruuvien kiristys. Muut tarvittavat korjaukset tehdään tarvittaessa lisätyönä. Urakka sisältää kaikki työt ja tarvikkeet valmiin lopputuloksen saavuttamiseksi sekä uuden lukituskaavion. Uuden lukituskaavion lisäksi laaditaan yhteisistä tiloista päivitetyt sijoituspohjapiirrokset tilaajalle. Lukituskaaviot ja uudet avaimet toimitetaan avainhallintapisteisiin (huoltoyhtiö/lukkoliike). Lukostojen laajuus on vanhan lukoston mukainen seuraavin huomautuksin: - avaimia 3 kpl / avaintyypit asunto, lehdenjakaja, reitti, kerhohuone jne. - huoltoavaimia 7 kpl, joista 1kpl toimitetaan KTL1E järjestelmän avainsäilöön - yleisavaimia 7 kpl - kaikki avaimet leimataan (yksilöity tunnus) - lukoston käytettävissä olevan reservin tulee olla mahdollisimman laaja Avaimet toimitetaan avainhallintapisteeseen viimeistään 14vrk (2 viikkoa) ennen sovitun asennusajan aloittamista TELETILOJEN SARJOITUS KTL1E Lisäksi kaikkien kiinteistöjen yhteiset teletilat sarjoitetaan KTL1E-järjestelmään ja rakennuksien ulkoseinään asennetaan KTL1E järjestelmän avainpesä (mikäli tyhjiä paikkoja ei ole, kuuluu avainsäilöputken seinään poraaminen myös urakkaan). Yhteisiä teletiloja ovat talojakamot, alijakamot, kerrosjakamot ja yhteisiin tiloihin asennetut kytkentäpaikkoja tai telelaitteita sisältävät muut ovelliset kotelot ja rasiat. KTL1E-avainsäilöputkeen toimitetaan 1kpl kohteen huoltoavaimia. Kaksi avainsäilön käyttöavainta toimitetaan muiden avaimien mukana avainhallintapisteeseen. KTL1E järjestelmän liittymismaksuista vastaa tilaaja. TIEDOTTAMINEN Tiedotteet töiden aloittamisesta (kohdekohtaisesti) tehdään yhteistyössä tilaajan kanssa viimeistään 3 viikkoa ennen asennustöiden aloittamista. description: Lukituksen uusiminen (16 kohdetta) MEKAANINEN LUKITUS Sarjoituksen kohteena on 16 asuinkiinteistöä. Kohteiden lukitus uusitaan mekaanisella järjestelmällä esim. Abloy Easy. Sylinterit uusitaan, vanhat lukkorungot ja helat säilytetään. Urakoitsija on velvollinen tutustumaan kohteisiin omatoimisesti ennen tarjouksen antamista ja varmistamaan lukituskaavioiden ajantasaisuus. Jätekatokset, piharakennukset, postilaatikot yms. lukitukset kuuluvat urakkaan kohteissa, joissa nämä ovat ennestäänkin lukittuja. Urakkaan kuuluu lisäksi lukkojen telkien ja avainpesien (käyttölukot, varmuuslukot, pitkäsalvat) voitelu ja ruuvien kiristys. Muut tarvittavat korjaukset tehdään tarvittaessa lisätyönä. Urakka sisältää kaikki työt ja tarvikkeet valmiin lopputuloksen saavuttamiseksi sekä uuden lukituskaavion. Uuden lukituskaavion lisäksi laaditaan yhteisistä tiloista päivitetyt sijoituspohjapiirrokset tilaajalle. Lukituskaaviot ja uudet avaimet toimitetaan avainhallintapisteisiin (huoltoyhtiö/lukkoliike). Lukostojen laajuus on vanhan lukoston mukainen seuraavin huomautuksin: - avaimia 3 kpl / avaintyypit asunto, lehdenjakaja, reitti, kerhohuone jne. - huoltoavaimia 7 kpl, joista 1kpl toimitetaan KTL1E järjestelmän avainsäilöön - yleisavaimia 7 kpl - kaikki avaimet leimataan (yksilöity tunnus) - lukoston käytettävissä olevan reservin tulee olla mahdollisimman laaja Avaimet toimitetaan avainhallintapisteeseen viimeistään 14vrk (2 viikkoa) ennen sovitun asennusajan aloittamista TELETILOJEN SARJOITUS KTL1E Lisäksi kaikkien kiinteistöjen yhteiset teletilat sarjoitetaan KTL1E-järjestelmään ja rakennuksien ulkoseinään asennetaan KTL1E järjestelmän avainpesä (mikäli tyhjiä paikkoja ei ole, kuuluu avainsäilöputken seinään poraaminen myös urakkaan). Yhteisiä teletiloja ovat talojakamot, alijakamot, kerrosjakamot ja yhteisiin tiloihin asennetut kytkentäpaikkoja tai telelaitteita sisältävät muut ovelliset kotelot ja rasiat. KTL1E-avainsäilöputkeen toimitetaan 1kpl kohteen huoltoavaimia. Kaksi avainsäilön käyttöavainta toimitetaan muiden avaimien mukana avainhallintapisteeseen. KTL1E järjestelmän liittymismaksuista vastaa tilaaja. title: Finland – Adult and other education services – Työntekijäksi teollisuuteen! Teollisuuden osaamis- ja täydennyskoulutukset työvoimakoulutuksena/ Pohjoisen Keski-Suomen työllisyysalue
description: Pohjoisen Keski-Suomen työllisyysalue pyytää tarjouksia tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden ja HILMA-ilmoituskanavassa julkaistun hankintailmoituksen työvoimapalveluiden järjestämislain (380/2023) luvun 7 mukaisista työvoimakoulutuksista, joiden olisi tarkoitus alkaa arviolta loppuvuonna 2026. Tarjouspyyntö ja sen liitteet ovat kaikilta osin tarjoajaa sitovia. Hankinta toteutetaan puitejärjestelynä. Puitejärjestelyyn valitaan osa-alueittain enintään yksi palveluntuottaja. Puitejärjestelyyn valinta oikeuttaa palveluntuottajan vastaanottamaan tilaajan tekemiä koulutustilauksia sopimuskauden aikana, mutta ei anna palveluntuottajalle oikeutta ennalta määrättyyn koulutusmäärään tai hankinnan arvoon. Hankinta koostuu kahdesta (2) pääteemasta, jotka kilpailutetaan tarjouspyynnössä erillisenä osakokonaisuutena. Nämä pääteemat ovat: - Kone- ja tuotantotekniikka - Prosessiteollisuus Hankinnan määrä on yhteensä 2500 opiskelijatyöpäivää (otp) sopimuskaudella. Koulutuksesta maksetaan toteutuneiden opiskelijatyöpäivien mukaan. Hankinta sisältää myös tulospalkkion. Hankinnan arvioitu sopimusaika on 1.12.2026 - 31.12.2027. Hankintaan liittyy optiomahdollisuus kahteen (2) yhden (1) vuoden pituisiin sopimuskausiin kolmen (3) vuoden kulussa alkuperäisen hankintasopimuksen laatimisesta. Option käyttöönotosta päättää tilaaja. Option käyttöönotosta ilmoitetaan palveluntuottajalle viimeistään kolme kuukautta ennen optiokauden alkua. Hankinnassa voidaan sopia tarvittaessa lisäostosta, joka on enintään 50 % alkuperäisen hankinnan arvosta. Lisäostoa voidaan käyttää kullakin sopimuskaudella opiskelijatyöpäivä määrien ylityksiin tai sopimuskaudella alkaneiden koulutusten jatko-osuuksiin (ns. hännät). Tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevassa palvelukuvauksessa on tarkemmat tiedot palvelun sisällöstä. Tarjouspyynnössä esitetyt hankintamäärät ovat arvioita, eivätkä ne muodosta hankintayksikölle määräostovelvoitetta. Palvelun siirtyminen, peruuntuminen tai hankkimatta jättäminen ei aiheuta hankintayksikölle korvausvelvollisuutta.

title: Finland – Furniture – Irtokalusteet
description: Numera yhteishankintapalvelut pyytää tarjoustanne irtokalusteista tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaan. Hankinta sisältää julkisten organisaatioiden uudis- ja peruskorjauskohteiden sekä täydennyshankintoina hankittavat irtokalusteet. Irtokalusteita hankitaan esimerkiksi toimistojen, koulujen, päiväkotien ja kirjastojen tarpeisiin. Hankinta on jaettu kolmeen osakokonaisuuteen: 1. Toimisto- ja julkitilakalusteet 2. Oppilas- ja koulukalusteet 3. Varhaiskasvatuksen kalusteet Kukin hankintakokonaisuus voidaan puitesopimuksen osakokonaisuusjaosta riippumatta hankkia samalta sopimustoimittajalta. Tällaisessa tilanteessa Tilaaja arvioi yksittäisen hankintakokonaisuuden pääasiallisen sisällön ja toimintaympäristön perusteella, minkä osakokonaisuuden perusteella hankinta tehdään (esimerkiksi koulukalustehankinnassa voidaan hankkia myös kyseiseen kouluun tulevia toimistokalusteita Oppilas- ja koulukalusteiden osakokonaisuuden toimittajalta). Kilpailutus suoritetaan avoimella menettelyllä, jonka perusteella puitejärjestelyn osakokonaisuuksiin 1 ja 2 valitaan toimittajaksi kuusi (6) ja osakokonaisuuteen 3 viisi (5) eniten pisteitä saanutta tarjoajaa, ellei hyväksyttävän tarjouksen jättäneitä tarjoajia ole vähemmän. Kilpailutuksen valintaperusteena on kokonaistaloudellinen edullisuus hinnan painoarvon ollessa 80 % ja laadun painoarvon ollessa 20 %. Sopimuskausi on määräaikainen neljä (4) vuotta. Sopimuskausi alkaa aikaisintaan hankintapäätöksen saatua lainvoiman tai markkinaoikeuden annettua sopimukselle täytäntöönpanoluvan. Sopimuksen irtisanomisaika on molempien sopijapuolten ja hankintaan sitoutuneiden Numera Palvelut Oy:n asiakasyhteisöjen osalta kuusi (6) kuukautta määräaikaisuudesta huolimatta. Tavoitteena on, että sopimuskausi astuu voimaan joulukuussa 2026. Kansallisen kynnysarvon alittavat hankinnat voi tehdä miltä tahansa osakokonaisuuden sopimustoimittajalta. Kansallisen kynnysarvon ylittävistä hankinnoista tehdään kevennetty kilpailutus. Kaikki hankinnassa mukana olevat yhteisöt on lueteltu sopimusluonnoksen liitteessä 1.

title: Finland – Substation construction work – Upalinkon 110 kV:n sähköaseman uusiminen
description: Turku Energia Sähköverkot Oy (jäljempänä TESV) uudistaa Turussa sijaitsevan Upalinkon 110 kV:n sähköaseman. Hankkeen lähtökohtana on nykyisen 110 kV:n avokytkinlaitoksen korvaaminen uudella SF6-kaasuvapaalla GIS-kytkinlaitoksella. Uusi kytkinlaitos sijoitetaan tämän hankinnan yhteydessä rakennettavaan sähköasemarakennukseen nykyisen sähköasema-alueen luoteisosaan. Olemassa olevat johtolähdöt liitetään uuteen kytkinlaitokseen nykyiseltä pääteportaalilta toteutettavilla 110 kV:n kaapeliyhteyksillä. Hankinnan kohteena on sähköaseman uusimista koskeva rakennusurakka, joka sisältää sähköaseman suunnittelun, rakentamisen, kojeistot ja muut materiaalit, asennus-, koestus- ja käyttöönottotyöt, dokumentoinnin sekä purkutyöt hankinta-asiakirjoissa tarkemmin määriteltävässä laajuudessa. Kyseessä on kokonaisvastuu-urakkana toteutettava hankinta. Hankinnassa noudatetaan F-kaasuasetuksen (EU) 2024/573 määräyksiä. Hankintaan sisältyvät pääkokonaisuudet ovat: - uuden kaksikerroksisen sähköasemarakennuksen rakentaminen; - 110 kV:n kaksikiskoinen GIS-kytkinlaitos sekä siihen liittyvät ohjaus-, suojaus-, automaatio- ja apusähköjärjestelmät; - 110 kV:n kaapelointityöt maa- ja perustustöineen sekä materiaaleineen; - nykyisen 110 kV:n avokojeiston ja asemarakennuksen purkutyöt. Hankinta toteutetaan erityisalojen hankintalain mukaisella neuvottelumenettelyllä. Koska hankinta liittyy tilaajan kriittiseen infrastruktuuriin, osallistumispyyntövaiheessa julkaistaan rajoitetusti hankintakokonaisuutta koskevat yleiset tiedot. Tämän osallistumispyynnön liitteenä toimitetaan hankekuvaus, alustava sopimusluonnos, referenssilomake, salassapitosopimus ja Rakennusurakan yleiset sopimusehdot YSE 1998. Tarjoajien tulee arvioida kiinnostuksensa osallistua hankintamenettelyyn osallistumispyynnössä ja sen liitteissä esitettyjen tietojen perusteella. Tarjoajan edellytetään hyväksyvän osallistumispyynnön liitteenä toimitettavan hanketta koskevan salassapitosopimuksen ja palauttavan sen allekirjoitettuna osallistumishakemuksen liitteenä. Tarjouskilpailuun valituille ehdokkaille toimitetaan hankintamenettelyn myöhemmissä vaiheissa tarkemmat tiedot hankinnan kohteesta. Hankinnan lopullinen sisältö, laajuus, rajapinnat sekä osapuolten vastuunjako täsmennetään tarjouskilpailun ja neuvottelujen aikana. Hankkeen toteutusvaiheen arvioidaan sijoittuvan vuosille 2027–2030. Suunnittelutyö voi käynnistyä sopimuksen tullessa voimaan ja rakennustyöt välittömästi, kun asianmukaiset luvat ovat lainvoimaisia. Uuden sähköaseman on tavoitteena valmistua tuotantokäyttöön 1.12.2029 mennessä ja hankkeeseen liittyvät purkutyöt tehdään 1.6.2030 mennessä. Aikataulu täsmentyy hankinnan valmistelun, neuvottelumenettelyn ja valittavan toteutusratkaisun perusteella.

description: ARCHITECT-ENGINEER (A-E) REQUEST FOR STANDARD FORM (SF) 330 QUALIFICATION PACKAGES THIS IS AN ARCHITECT-ENGINEER (A-E) PRESOLICITATION NOTICE AND A REQUEST FOR STANDARD FORM (SF) 330 QUALIFICATION PACKAGES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PRICE PROPOSALS. Project Description The U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC), Office of Facilities and Environmental Quality (OFEQ), Building Management Division (BMD), intends to award up to three (3) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Architect-Engineer (A-E) contracts to provide comprehensive multi-disciplinary architectural and engineering services in support of renovation, modernization, repair, and infrastructure improvement projects at the historic Herbert C. Hoover Building (HCHB) in Washington, DC. The resulting contracts will provide professional planning, facility assessments, engineering investigations, design services, technical studies, cost estimating, and construction phase services for projects throughout the HCHB. As the headquarters of the Department of Commerce and a historically significant Federal facility, the HCHB requires the careful integration of modern building systems while preserving its historic character and ensuring compliance with applicable Federal laws, building codes, life safety requirements, accessibility standards, sustainability objectives, and historic preservation requirements. The Building Management Division (BMD) is responsible for the operation, maintenance, repair, and modernization of the HCHB's critical building systems, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC); electrical distribution; plumbing; steam; structural; fire protection; environmental; and vertical transportation (elevator) systems. Task orders issued under the resulting IDIQ contracts may require one or multiple engineering disciplines depending on the scope and complexity of each project. Services shall include work in areas to: Architectural Design Structural Engineering Mechanical Engineering Electrical Engineering Plumbing Engineering Civil Engineering Fire Protection Engineering Environmental Engineering Facility Planning Utility Infrastructure Design Cost Estimating Building Condition Assessments Failure Investigations Destructive and Non-Destructive Testing Stormwater Management Water and Sanitary Utility Systems Interior Renovation Design Technical Studies and Engineering Assessments Projects may range from minor facility renovations to complex infrastructure modernization efforts and may involve single-discipline or multidisciplinary engineering services. Given the broad range of potential work and the importance of understanding existing site conditions, the Government is requiring prospective offerors to attend a mandatory site visit. Offerors must register for the site visit using the provided Microsoft Forms link in this announcement. The visit will provide an opportunity to review site conditions and ask questions regarding the scope and technical requirements. Questions may be raised during the mandatory site visit. Oral responses are provided for general informational purposes and do not revise the public announcement. Questions and answers that materially clarify or affect the project requirements, submission instructions, or selection criteria will be issued in writing to all firms through an update to the public announcement. Firms shall rely only on the written announcement and any written updates issued by the Contracting Officer. Firms are responsible for ensuring their small business status is current and accurately reflected in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov). Estimated Program Value: The estimated cumulative ordering ceiling for all contracts awarded under this procurement is: $9,889,921.79. A&E Selection Criteria and Relative Importance: In accordance with 40 U.S.C. Chapter 11, Selection of Architects and Engineers (Brooks Architect-Engineer Act) and RFO FAR Part 36, the Government will evaluate firms based on demonstrated competence and professional qualifications. The evaluation will focus on the firm's specialized experience and technical competence in the following disciplines. Firms shall demonstrate the capability to provide A-E services in the following required disciplines: Electrical Engineering Mechanical Engineering Civil Engineering Fire Protection Engineering Environmental Engineering Architectural Design The Government will evaluate the qualifications and capabilities of the entire proposed team, including the prime firm and any proposed consultants or subcontractors identified in the SF 330. 1. Specialized Experience � Most Important The Government will evaluate the firm's specialized experience and technical competence based on the relevance, similarity, and complexity of prior A-E projects submitted in the SF 330. The evaluation will consider the extent to which the firm's demonstrated experience includes: A-E services similar in scope, size, complexity, and technical requirements to this requirement; Single-discipline and multi-disciplinary projects involving the required A-E disciplines; Renovation, modernization, repair, and infrastructure improvement projects involving existing facilities; and Experience demonstrating the firm's ability to successfully perform the types of A-E services anticipated under this IDIQ. Firms shall demonstrate their Specialized Experience through relevant projects submitted in SF 330, Part I, Section F � Example Projects Which Best Illustrate Proposed Team's Qualifications for This Contract. Firms shall submit 3 relevant projects performed within the past 5 years from the date of this announcement. Specialized Experience will be evaluated using the following confidence ratings: The Government has LOW CONFIDENCE that the Offeror understands the requirement, proposes a sound approach or will be successful in performing the contract even with Government intervention. The Government has SOME CONFIDENCE that the offeror understands the requirement, proposes a sound approach, and will be successful in performing the contract with some Government intervention. The Government has HIGH CONFIDENCE that the offeror understands the requirement, proposes a sound approach, and will be successful in performing the contract with little or no Government intervention. 2. Professional Qualifications � Second Most Important The Government will evaluate the Professional Qualifications of the key personnel proposed to perform the required A-E services. Firms shall identify and submit the proposed key personnel in SF 330, Part I, Section E � Resumes of Key Personnel Proposed for This Contract, consistent with the key personnel positions identified in the Functional Requirements. The Government will evaluate the relevance, depth, and adequacy of the proposed key personnel's professional qualifications in relation to their proposed roles and the A-E services required under this IDIQ. The evaluation will consider, as applicable: Education; Years and type of relevant professional experience; Professional registrations and licenses; Professional certifications; Technical qualifications; and Relevant individual project experience. The six required A-E disciplines are encompassed within the applicable personnel categories identified in the Functional Requirements, including Program/Project Manager, Senior Engineer/Architect/Specialist, and Project Engineer/Architect. title: Engineering Services and Support Related to the Convair 580 Aircraft
description: The National Research Council’s (NRC) Flight Research Laboratory (FRL) operates a Convair 580 aircraft for flight research. As the aircraft is frequently modified and/or operated in a manner different to the original design purpose, engineering support from the holder of the aircraft’s Type design and intellectual property is frequently required. As a result, the FRL requires a 5-year Standing Offer to provide engineering services and support related to the Convair 580 aircraft. This work will involve: Order of raw materials, machining of raw materials for hardpoint and pylon, engineering studies and/or modifications to the Convair 580 to support external sensors, on-going maintenance/repair and technical support, engineering analysis for flight loads, aerodynamics, flight test, Component manufacture and/or provision of design/manufacturing data to NRC, pylon completion, fit out, finishing and procurement of additional components/parts necessary for continued operation of the Convair 580. Additional services/parts not listed may be required to support the modification of the Convair 580.

title: Active Vibration Isolation System compatible with a Thermo Fisher Scientific Verios 5 Ultra High Resolution Scanning Electron Microscope (UHR-SEM)
description: The High Temperature Materials Group in the Structures and Materials Performance Laboratory of the National Research Council’s (NRC) Aerospace (AERO-SMPL-HTM) requires an active vibration isolation (AVI) system to achieve the required performance of the group’s ultra-high resolution scanning electron microscope (UHR-SEM). AERO-SMPL-HTM uses its UHR-SEM in advanced research on a wide range of materials for various applications. However, the instrument cannot provide the highest possible image resolution due to significant low-frequency disturbances during high-magnification imaging. A new AVI system will effectively dampen mechanical vibrations and eliminate disruptive low-frequency vibration noise that interferes with image acquisition. The new system will allow the UHR-SEM to achieve its optimum performance, and enhance AERO-SMPL’s capability to conduct advanced research and provide data for a large number of the research projects.

title: Modular Wind Power for Northern Operations
description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness levels (TRL) 1-9 can be submitted to this challenge. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/016 - Modular Wind Power For North Operations The Department of National Defence and Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) are seeking innovative solutions to develop modular, stand-alone wind-powered electric generator systems that can be easily transported, deployed, and maintained in remote northern locations to provide reliable, clean energy under extreme cold, high-wind, and icing conditions. Background & Context The demand for electrical power and space heating in the Canadian Subarctic and High Arctic is fulfilled almost exclusively with diesel-fired generators. The DND/CAF is seeking to reduce reliance on fossil fuels for the generation of electrical power in the North to minimize operational, logistical, and environmental burdens. Wind turbines suitable for DND/CAF operations are in limited use in the North, as existing installations tend to fall outside the desired capacity range. While small units that deliver up to 6 kilowatts (kW) have been deployed in some communities, and commercial turbines typically exceed 1 megawatt (MW), there is a critical gap in the 25–100 kW range—an ideal scale for remote DND sites. In addition, northern operating conditions present major technical and environmental hurdles that must be overcome before wind turbines can be fully exploited as a source of alternative energy. Canada's far North and Arctic regions are characterized by seasonally frozen ground, deep snow, rugged terrain, permafrost, and extreme temperatures that can reach –60 degrees Celsius (°C), with frequent high winds of 80–120 kilometers per hour (km/h). Ice rimming of wind turbine blades further threatens performance and efficiency. Innovative approaches are therefore needed to adapt conventional wind-powered electric generator designs to withstand these harsh northern conditions and operate effectively under both low and high wind scenarios. Climate change adds additional complexity, as thawing and refreezing permafrost can cause buildings and foundations to sink, shift, or crack. While not the primary focus of the challenge, consideration must be given to the design of the foundations to keep the turbines level and stable despite seasonal ground movement. There is a need for wind-powered electricity generators that are logistically efficient, easy to deploy, and maintainable in isolated northern locations. Many DND/CAF sites exist in remote areas or within small Arctic communities that have limited or no road access and must be reached by alternative means of transportation such as barges or heavy-lift aircraft. Consequently, new systems must feature modular designs that can be transported and assembled on site with minimal heavy-lift equipment by non-technicians using commonly available tools. To ensure sustained operation, proposed solutions should use readily available parts, be serviceable by local tradespeople, and operate with minimal human intervention once deployed. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Provide a design for a wind-powered electrical generation system in the 25–100 kW range, incorporating details of the structural, mechanical, electrical, and control elements required. • Provide integration and operational demonstration plan(s), showing how the wind-powered electric generator system can function in remote northern locations and operate and withstand northern environmental conditions, including extreme cold (down to –60 °C), high winds (up to 120 km/h), and icing conditions without intervention. • Integrate with existing electrical power systems or microgrids and must enable coordinated operation with other energy sources and support performance under varying generation and load conditions. • Use a modular design that allows transport by air or ship — ensuring that individual components fit within a standard 20ft sea container with maximum dimensions of 108 in. (2.74 m) wide × 268 in. (6.81 m) long × 96 in. (2.44 m) high and a maximum weight of 24,000 lb (10,886 kg; 10.9 tonnes). • The modular design must enable onsite assembly without the need for heavy lift equipment. • Support maintainability and repairability in northern environments by ensuring the wind powered electric generator system can be serviced using standard mechanical and electrical tools, without reliance on specialized proprietary equipment or manufacturer field support. Desired Outcomes Proposed solutions should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Electromagnetic interference that complies with MIL STD 461G, Department of Defense Interface Standard for the Control of Electromagnetic Interference Characteristics of Subsystems and Equipment. • Foundation design that accounts for Arctic ground conditions, including permafrost, active-layer variation, and freeze-thaw effects, over the intended design life of the generator.

title: Sustainable Northern Operations: Water & Waste
description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/018 - Sustainable Northern Operations: Water & Waste The Department of National Defence and the Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) are seeking novel, integrated technologies that enable the CAF to operate Relocatable Transportable Camps (RTCs) independently and sustainably in Arctic and sub-Arctic environments while meeting all applicable Canadian environmental and health regulations. Background and context The CAF’s strategic update Our North, Strong and Free (2024) directs an expansion of military operations in the Canadian North. RTCs deployed in remote Arctic regions must sustain personnel with safe water, sanitation, and waste-handling capabilities while minimizing logistics and environmental risk. In 2023, the IDEaS Pop-Up City contest demonstrated advanced, containerized power-water-waste systems. These prototypes significantly reduced solid-waste mass and potable-water demand but were not tested under Arctic winter conditions. Material brittleness, freezing of fluids, and power-efficiency issues remain key obstacles. This challenge will bridge this gap by developing, and then testing integrated cold-weather water and waste technologies under Arctic winter conditions (e.g., Op NANOOK). The objective of the challenge is to support the development of a proven, deployable, Canadian-made, Arctic-ready water-and-waste system enabling CAF RTCs to operate independently, safely, and sustainably in the North with drastically reduced logistics burden and environmental impact. Essential outcomes Proposed solutions must meet the following requirements: • Integrated capability combining water purification, wastewater treatment and solid-waste reduction suitable for camps of up to 50 personnel. • Use a modular design that allows transport by air or ship – ensuring that individual components fit within a standard 20 ft sea container with maximum dimensions of 108 in. (2.74 m) wide × 268 in. (6.81 m) long × 96 in. (2.44 m) high and a maximum weight of 24,000 lb (10,886 kg; 10.9 tonnes). The modular design must also enable on site assembly without the need for heavy lift equipment. • Treated outputs must meet or exceed Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and Health Canada Drinking-Water Guidelines. • Function continuously in remote northern locations and operate and withstand northern environmental conditions, including extreme cold down to -40°C. • Resource efficiency must be demonstrated through a reduction in resupply volume and frequency (water, consumables) by at least 75% from baseline (see Table 1 below). • Support maintainability and repairability in northern environments by ensuring that the solution can be serviced using common trades and tools available to CAF in deployed operations in remote areas. Desired outcomes Proposed solutions should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Integrated power. • Operable in extreme heat conditions (up to +40°C). • No manual pre-processing of solid waste. • Recovery and reuse of waste-heat or by-products. • Can be scaled to suit camps of over 50 personnel, up to 1500 personnel. Table 1. Baseline for resources requirements for consumption and management per volume and frequency. Resource Volume and Frequency Potable water‡ 150 L / person / day Non-potable water 50 L / person / day Sewage – Black water 89.5 L / person / day Sewage – Grey water 48.5 L / person / day Solid waste – Dry* 1.1 kg / person / day Solid waste – Wet† 1.1 kg / person / day ‡ Water supplied to RTC at =4°C. 20% of potable water requirement (i.e. 30 L/person/day), is used as hot water at 60°C. * Total energy content can be assumed to be 15 MJ/kg. † Water content can be assumed to be 70%.

title: PR19224 - 47419-269614 - Chemical Detection Systems ITQ - List of Qualified Respondents
description: On June 11, 2025, Canada issued an Invitation to Qualify (ITQ) (Solicitation CW2405177 / Client Ref No. 1000519614 – 47419-269614) allowing for Interested Parties to pre-qualify for Chemical Detection Systems in 4 streams. Stream 1 – Ion Mobility Spectrometers (IMS); Stream 2 – Infrared Spectrometers (IR), Stream 3 – Mass Spectrometers (MS), and Stream 4 – Raman Spectrometers (Raman). At this time, only the listed QRs will be invited to participate in the subsequent phases of the Chemical Detection Systems procurement process.
